The statement correctly preserves genus under a separable algebraic extension of the exact constant field, including an infinite extension. The [rendered theorem and proof](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/ConstantExtension/Genus.lean#L269) assume a genuine one-variable function field, `IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F`, and that the [actual compositum](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/GeometricDegree.lean#L113) is all of `F'`. `Algebra.IsSeparable k k'` entails algebraicity here; there is no finite-dimensionality assumption on the constant extension. Exactness is essential: it prevents the genus definition from measuring dimensions against a smaller, incorrect constant field. The proof compares degrees and Riemann–Roch dimensions of positive multiples of a pole divisor, so it does not use the junk natural finrank of an infinite extension.

The exact-name search was supplemented by the [Layer 8 target](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicCurves/README.md#L791). Its perfect-field case follows because algebraic extensions of a perfect field are separable. The explicitly required inseparable counterexample is present with proofs: [exact constants and genus `(p−1)/2`](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/ConstantExtension/InseparableGenusDrop.lean#L188), the actual [constant-compositum equality](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/ConstantExtension/InseparableGenusDrop.lean#L211), and [strict genus drop](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/ConstantExtension/InseparableGenusDrop.lean#L234) for odd prime characteristic. Thus the excluded inseparable case is mathematically substantive. Broader Layer 8 ramification, divisor-class, and Clifford milestones are separate conclusions. These checks were inspected in source without `sorry`; I have not obtained a successful local Lean rebuild. No existing review reason was present in the downloaded entry.

The rendered statement agrees with the [pinned theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/RingTheory/DedekindDomain/Discriminant/Ramification.lean#L39): for a nonzero prime p of A, divisibility of the relative discriminant is equivalent to failure of unramifiedness at some prime of B above p. Finite torsion-free Dedekind extension and separable fraction fields are explicit. The [definition](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/RingTheory/DedekindDomain/Discriminant/Basic.lean#L33) is the relative norm of the different, and the proof combines prime divisibility of that norm with the different's local unramifiedness criterion. In particular it does not silently replace unramifiedness by ramification index one when residue fields could be inseparable.

The [Completed/NumberFieldArithmetic checks](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/Completed/NumberFieldArithmetic/README.md#L1189) explicitly require this distinction, the identity-extension edge case, and agreement with the usual number-field discriminant. I checked the proved [identity discriminant = unit ideal](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/RingTheory/DedekindDomain/Discriminant/Basic.lean#L49), [absolute-discriminant ideal comparison](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/Discriminant/Relative.lean#L37), and [number-field e > 1 corollary](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/Discriminant/Ramification.lean#L36). The latter uses residue-field separability and matches the classical number-field criterion in [Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, Theorem 3.35](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/ANT.pdf#page=62). Inseparable fraction-field extensions, whose different/discriminant may vanish, are intentionally outside this theorem. Tower formulas elsewhere in the milestone are separate results. The inspected rendered record contained the naming announcement, not a prior substantive review. Verification here is source inspection, without a successful local Lean rebuild.
